findings.summary: The new tests' source of truth is the ROOT settings.gradle.kts, which is neither a declared Gradle input nor in check-harness-tests.sh's delta pathspec. RuleListTest, ModulePlanTest and ModuleListDerivationTest therefore do not run on the change they guard. The diff widens the input declaration to scripts/*.sh but leaves the other file these tests read undeclared.
findings.failure_scenario: Rename `ingest` to `ingester` in settings.gradle.kts and rename the directory. Stage settings.gradle.kts + ingester/build.gradle.kts + the moved sources. check-harness-tests.sh runs delta and evaluates `changed_files 'scripts/*.py' 'scripts/*.sh' 'buildSrc/*'` -- verified: settings.gradle.kts matches none of those pathspecs -- so it prints `ok no harness change; suite not run` and never starts Gradle. RuleListTest, whose entire purpose is 'rename a module and its rule silently stops applying', does not execute. check-module.sh runs (shared-build escalation, 8 modules) and passes, because NO_HTTP still names the dead module `ingest` and simply never matches `ingester`: architecture.md rule 5 stops applying to the ingester and the gate prints ok. Even if the suite were invoked, buildSrc's Test task declares only scripts/*.py|*.sh and buildSrc/src/test/resources as inputs, so it reports UP-TO-DATE. Same mechanism for the more likely case of ADDING a ninth module: ModulePlanTest's `ALL=<eight names>` and `DRIFT=ok checked=8` assertions go stale silently and surface later attached to an unrelated commit that happens to touch scripts/. Fix is two lines: add 'settings.gradle.kts' and '*/build.gradle.kts' to the pathspec at scripts/check-harness-tests.sh:21, and add the root settings.gradle.kts to inputs.files in buildSrc/build.gradle.kts.

findings.summary: The hook comment points the reader at `build.md § Execution layers`, but the cost narrative and the 11 s/15 s non-measurement it defers to were added under `§ Gate scope: fast by default, complete in CI` (build.md:83). § Execution layers is at build.md:128 and contains only the L0-L5 budget table.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer whose commit suddenly takes seconds follows the pointer, lands on the L0-L5 table, finds no mention of check-module, of the shared-build cliff, or of the unmeasured cold-daemon case, and concludes the numbers were deleted rather than relocated -- then restates a measured number in the hook comment, which is the two-copies drift the comment exists to prevent.

findings.summary: RuleListTest is a real constraint but a one-directional one: `isSubsetOf(all)` catches a rule naming a DEAD module (rename, typo) and catches NO_HTTP="" (the split yields [""], not in `all`). It does not catch a rule that stops naming a LIVE module, which is the weakening a developer under pressure actually performs.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer wants Helidon in `ingest`, hits `ingest resolves an HTTP dependency (architecture.md rule 5, ADR-0019)`, and edits scripts/check-module.sh:221 to NO_HTTP="format binstore-spi sequencer". Both RuleListTest cases stay green (a shorter list is still a subset, and the lists are still disjoint), check-module.sh prints `ok 8 module(s) checked`, and rule 5 is off for the one module the gate's own comment says it must cover. That is non-negotiable 2 -- a threshold moved in the direction that weakens its gate -- with no detector. Same family as M0.23; the honest fix is to widen M0.23's row to include 'a rule list that stops naming a live module', or to say so in the javadoc, which currently reads as though list integrity is covered.
